exposure: irregular vaginal bleeding for more than three months
outcome: position of the internal os of the cervix on MRI images
ability to locate the internal os of the cervix by MRI
cohort: The cohort consisted of 175 patients who underwent total hysterectomy for stage I endometrial cancer.
finding: The study confirmed that the position of the internal os of the cervix on MRI images was consistent with removed uterus specimens, and identified that a history of cesarean section, irregular vaginal bleeding for more than three months, cervical adenomyosis, and premenopause were not conducive to locating the internal os by MRI.
mod_finding: A history of cesarean section was identified as a factor not conducive to accurately locating the internal os of the cervix by MRI.
